questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice of: 'She writes a letter every day.'
options: A letter is written by her every day.
A letter was written by her every day.
A letter has been written by her every day.
A letter will be written by her every day.
questions.explanation: Simple Present active (writes) → Simple Present passive: is/am/are + past participle. 'She' becomes 'her' after 'by'. Options B/C/D shift tense wrongly.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice of: 'The teacher punished the student.'
options: The student is punished by the teacher.
The student was punished by the teacher.
The student had been punished by the teacher.
The student has been punished by the teacher.
questions.explanation: Simple Past active (punished) → Simple Past passive: was/were + past participle. 'was punished' is correct. Option A uses present, C uses past perfect, D uses present perfect.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct active voice of: 'A novel was written by her.'
options: She writes a novel.
She has written a novel.
She wrote a novel.
She had written a novel.
questions.explanation: Passive 'was written' (Simple Past passive) → active Simple Past: She wrote a novel. Options A/B/D use wrong tenses (present, present perfect, past perfect).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice of: 'They will complete the project by Friday.'
options: The project was completed by them by Friday.
The project has been completed by them by Friday.
The project is completed by them by Friday.
The project will be completed by them by Friday.
questions.explanation: Simple Future active (will complete) → Simple Future passive: will be + past participle. 'will be completed' is correct. Options A/B/C incorrectly use past or present forms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice of: 'The chef is preparing a special dish.'
options: A special dish is being prepared by the chef.
A special dish was being prepared by the chef.
A special dish has been prepared by the chef.
A special dish is prepared by the chef.
questions.explanation: Present Continuous active (is preparing) → Present Continuous passive: is/am/are + being + past participle. 'is being prepared' is correct. B uses past continuous, C uses present perfect, D uses simple present.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice of: 'He has submitted the report.'
options: The report was submitted by him.
The report has been submitted by him.
The report had been submitted by him.
The report is submitted by him.
questions.explanation: Present Perfect active (has submitted) → Present Perfect passive: has/have + been + past participle. 'has been submitted' is correct. A uses simple past, C uses past perfect, D uses simple present.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice of: 'The workers were building a bridge.'
options: A bridge was built by the workers.
A bridge is being built by the workers.
A bridge was being built by the workers.
A bridge had been built by the workers.
questions.explanation: Past Continuous active (were building) → Past Continuous passive: was/were + being + past participle. 'was being built' is correct. A uses simple past, B uses present continuous, D uses past perfect.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct active voice of: 'The message has been sent by the manager.'
options: The manager sends the message.
The manager sent the message.
The manager had sent the message.
The manager has sent the message.
questions.explanation: Present Perfect passive (has been sent) → Present Perfect active: has/have + past participle. 'The manager has sent the message' is correct. A uses simple present, B uses simple past, C uses past perfect.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice of: 'She had already locked the door.'
options: The door had already been locked by her.
The door has already been locked by her.
The door was already locked by her.
The door is already locked by her.
questions.explanation: Past Perfect active (had locked) → Past Perfect passive: had + been + past participle. 'had already been locked' is correct. B uses present perfect, C uses simple past, D uses simple present.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice of: 'They can solve this problem.'
options: This problem could be solved by them.
This problem can be solved by them.
This problem must be solved by them.
This problem will be solved by them.
questions.explanation: Modal 'can' active → modal passive: can + be + past participle. The modal itself does not change. Options A/C/D substitute a different modal, altering the meaning.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice of: 'You must follow the rules.'
options: The rules should be followed by you.
The rules might be followed by you.
The rules must be followed by you.
The rules can be followed by you.
questions.explanation: Modal 'must' active → modal passive: must + be + past participle. 'must be followed' preserves the obligatory meaning. Options A/B/D replace 'must' with different modals, changing the original sense.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice of: 'The mechanic did not repair the car.'
options: The car has not been repaired by the mechanic.
The car is not repaired by the mechanic.
The car had not been repaired by the mechanic.
The car was not repaired by the mechanic.
questions.explanation: Negative Simple Past active (did not repair) → Negative Simple Past passive: was/were + not + past participle. 'was not repaired' is correct. A/C shift to perfect tenses; B uses simple present.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct active voice of: 'The cake was baked by my mother.'
options: My mother baked the cake.
My mother bakes the cake.
My mother has baked the cake.
My mother was baking the cake.
questions.explanation: Simple Past passive (was baked) → Simple Past active: My mother baked the cake. Options B/C/D incorrectly use present simple, present perfect, and past continuous respectively.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice of: 'Did the students complete the assignment?'
options: Is the assignment completed by the students?
Was the assignment completed by the students?
Has the assignment been completed by the students?
Had the assignment been completed by the students?
questions.explanation: Interrogative Simple Past active (Did...complete?) → Simple Past passive interrogative: Was/Were + object + past participle? 'Was the assignment completed?' is correct. A uses present, C/D use perfect forms.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice of: 'She should learn this lesson.'
options: This lesson must be learnt by her.
This lesson would be learnt by her.
This lesson should be learnt by her.
This lesson shall be learnt by her.
questions.explanation: Modal 'should' active → modal passive: should + be + past participle. 'should be learnt' preserves the advisory sense. Options A/B/D substitute must/would/shall, each with a different meaning.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct active voice of: 'The thief was caught by the police.'
options: The police catches the thief.
The police has caught the thief.
The police caught the thief.
The police had caught the thief.
questions.explanation: Simple Past passive (was caught) → Simple Past active: The police caught the thief. Option A uses simple present, B uses present perfect, D uses past perfect — all wrong tenses.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice of: 'They will have finished the construction by December.'
options: The construction was finished by them by December.
The construction will be finished by them by December.
The construction has been finished by them by December.
The construction will have been finished by them by December.
questions.explanation: Future Perfect active (will have finished) → Future Perfect passive: will have been + past participle. 'will have been finished' is correct. A uses simple past, B uses simple future, C uses present perfect.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice of: 'Who broke the window?'
options: By whom was the window broken?
Whom was the window broken by?
Who was the window broken by?
By who was the window broken?
questions.explanation: When the active subject is 'Who', the passive uses 'By whom' (objective case). The auxiliary 'was' fronts the sentence: 'By whom was the window broken?' Option B is informal, C keeps 'Who' (wrong case), D uses 'who' after preposition (wrong case).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice of: 'The manager has asked him to submit the report.'
options: He had been asked to submit the report by the manager.
He has been asked to submit the report by the manager.
He was asked to submit the report by the manager.
He is asked to submit the report by the manager.
questions.explanation: Present Perfect active (has asked) with infinitive complement → Present Perfect passive: has been + past participle. The infinitive 'to submit' is retained unchanged. A uses past perfect, C uses simple past, D uses simple present.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice of: 'People believe that honesty is the best policy.'
options: Honesty is being believed to be the best policy.
Honesty was believed to be the best policy.
It is believed that honesty is the best policy.
People are believed to think honesty is the best policy.
questions.explanation: For verbs like believe/think/say/know with a 'that-clause', the impersonal passive is: 'It + is/was + past participle + that-clause'. 'It is believed that...' is correct. A is wrong because 'believe' is stative; B shifts to past; D has faulty structure.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice of: 'Let him do the work.'
options: The work should be done by him.
The work must be done by him.
Let him be done the work.
Let the work be done by him.
questions.explanation: Passive of 'Let + object + V1' is 'Let + object + be + V3'. So 'Let him do the work' → 'Let the work be done by him.' Options A/B replace the imperative with modal obligations; C is grammatically incorrect.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct active voice of: 'The decision was being debated by the committee when I arrived.'
options: The committee debated the decision when I arrived.
The committee was debating the decision when I arrived.
The committee had debated the decision when I arrived.
The committee has debated the decision when I arrived.
questions.explanation: Past Continuous passive (was being debated) → Past Continuous active: was/were + V-ing. 'The committee was debating the decision' correctly shows the ongoing action interrupted by 'I arrived'. Option A loses the ongoing aspect; C/D use perfect tenses.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice of: 'Someone has stolen my wallet.'
options: My wallet has been stolen.
My wallet was stolen.
My wallet had been stolen.
My wallet is stolen.
questions.explanation: Present Perfect active (has stolen) with indefinite subject 'someone' → Present Perfect passive: has/have + been + past participle. The agent phrase 'by someone' is omitted as it adds no information. B uses simple past, C uses past perfect, D uses simple present.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct active voice of: 'The bridge is being constructed by engineers.'
options: Engineers construct the bridge.
Engineers constructed the bridge.
Engineers have constructed the bridge.
Engineers are constructing the bridge.
questions.explanation: Present Continuous passive (is being constructed) → Present Continuous active: is/are + V-ing. 'Engineers are constructing the bridge' is correct. A uses simple present, B uses simple past, C uses present perfect.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice of: 'She could have won the prize.'
options: The prize could be won by her.
The prize would have been won by her.
The prize could have been won by her.
The prize should have been won by her.
questions.explanation: Modal perfect active (could have + V3) → Modal perfect passive: could have been + past participle. 'could have been won' is correct. A drops 'have', losing the perfect aspect; B/D substitute different modals (would/should).
questions.subject: English
